title: Tensor inclusion, image and kernel criterion for polynomial coefficient reduction
statement: Let $P$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq P$ an ideal, $A=P/I$, $m\geq0$, $Q=P[y_1,\ldots,y_m]$, and $C$ any commutative $A$-algebra. Let $\alpha:A[y_1,\ldots,y_m]\to C$ be an $A$-algebra map and $\varphi:Q\to C$ a surjective ring map equal to $\alpha\circ\pi$, where $\pi$ reduces coefficients modulo $I$. Put $H=\ker\pi$, $J=\ker\varphi$, and $M=I/I^2$. There is a $C$-linear map $i:C\otimes_A M\to J/J^2$, sending $c\otimes[x]$ to $c[\operatorname{C}(x)]$ for every $x\in I$. Its image, regarded as a $Q$-submodule of $J/J^2$, is the image of $H$ under the quotient map $J\to J/J^2$. Moreover, $i$ is injective if and only if $H\cap J^2=HJ$. Neither projectivity nor any condition on $\ker\alpha$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the proved polynomial coefficient tensor quotient identification to obtain a Q-linear equivalence from C tensor_A I/I² to H/HJ, with its representative formula.

Compatibility gives H ≤ J. Compose the inclusion H → J with J → J/J². It annihilates JH since JH ≤ J², so lift it to H/JH. Compose with the tensor identification. Surjectivity of Q → C upgrades Q-linearity to C-linearity. The representative formula follows from the quotient lift formula and the section identity.

Since both the tensor identification and H → H/JH are surjective, the range of the composite is the range of H → J/J², which is the required image. Injectivity is invariant under precomposition by the equivalence. If the quotient inclusion is injective, an element of H intersect J² represents zero and hence lies in HJ. Conversely, if H intersect J² = HJ, lift a kernel element to H; its vanishing in J/J² puts the representative in J² and therefore in HJ, so its quotient class is zero. The reverse ideal containment always holds.

theorem polynomial_coefficient_conormal_inclusion
    (P : Type u) [CommRing P] (I : Ideal P) (m : ℕ)
    (C : Type v) [CommRing C] [Algebra (P ⧸ I) C]
    (α : MvPolynomial (Fin m) (P ⧸ I) →ₐ[P ⧸ I] C)
    (φ : MvPolynomial (Fin m) P →+* C)
    (hφeq : φ = α.toRingHom.comp (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)))
    (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    ∃ (i : C ⊗[P ⧸ I] I.Cotangent →ₗ[C]
        (Extension.ofSurjective φ.toIntAlgHom hφ).Cotangent),
      (∀ (c : C) (x : I) (y : (Extension.ofSurjective φ.toIntAlgHom hφ).ker),
        y.1 = MvPolynomial.C x.1 →
          i (c ⊗ₜ I.toCotangent x) = c • Extension.Cotangent.mk y) ∧
      i.range.restrictScalars (Extension.ofSurjective φ.toIntAlgHom hφ).Ring =
        (Submodule.comap (Extension.ofSurjective φ.toIntAlgHom hφ).ker.subtype
          (RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)))).map
            Extension.Cotangent.mk ∧
      (Function.Injective i ↔
        RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)) ⊓
            (RingHom.ker φ) ^ 2 =
          RingHom.ker (MvPolynomial.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) (σ := Fin m)) *
            RingHom.ker φ)
